rule: Merge-write skill grants exactly merge-approved.sh by plugin-root path, runs no command, and the review watch invokes it right before every merge call, reporting a refused merge call as MERGE=skipped:permission-denied
description: plugin/skills/merge-write/SKILL.md is the model-only skill whose allowed-tools pre-approve the review watch's opt-in merge script for the rest of the turn that invokes it. A skill grant lasts only for the turn that invokes the skill, and the merge runs turns after hivemind:github-review-loop is invoked, so the watch skill holds no merge grant of its own and re-invokes merge-write in the merge call's own turn. The source pin holds the grant claim: its allowed-tools pre-approve exactly one script, by its plugin-root path, for the rest of the turn that invokes it. Three consumer pins in the same file hold the rest of the rule: the skill runs no command; the timing obligation, invoke it right before that call, after any other skill call; and the ban on any other skill invocation between the grant and the call. Two consumer pins in plugin/skills/github-review-loop/SKILL.md hold the watch side. The first carries the invocation: right before every merge call, in the same turn, invoke hivemind:merge-write with no other skill call between, and a refused Skill call does not skip the merge call. The second carries the fallback for a merge call the permission system refuses: it is reported as MERGE=skipped:permission-denied, routed like the other skipped lines with no retry, and its Next action names the per-machine allow rule for permissions.allow in .claude/settings.local.json. The set_check reads the top-level allowed-tools key with extract_frontmatter_key, which runs check16_collect_entries, the frontmatter reader CHECK 16 uses in tools/policy_check.sh, and requires, in equal mode with expected_counts, exactly the one Bash entry, once and in the double-quoted plugin-root form. An added or widened grant fails as an extra, a dropped grant fails as missing, and a duplicated grant fails its count. set_check is used because an added grant is the threat, and a presence pin can only notice deletion. What this fixture does not check: (a) the presence pins are whole-file, not section-scoped, so a pinned sentence that moves out of its section, such as the invoke sentence leaving the merge rule, stays green; (b) the grant set of plugin/skills/github-review-loop/SKILL.md is not checked, so a merge-approved.sh grant re-added there is invisible to this fixture; (c) a new skill or agent that grants or calls merge-approved.sh is an absence defect no presence pin can find; (d) the pins prove nothing about runtime grant behavior, such as whether Claude Code honors the skill's allowed-tools for the rest of the turn, whether the auto-mode classifier passes the call, or whether a deny, ask or managed-only rule overrides them; (e) files is a literal list that names only the merge-write skill and is blind to grants in any other skill or settings file; (f) surrounding prose can invert the meaning of a pinned sentence while its words stay intact, because a pin claims word-sequence presence, never meaning.

source.pattern: Its allowed-tools pre-approve exactly one script, by its plugin-root path, for the rest of the turn that invokes it

consumers.pattern: Invoke it right before that call, after any other skill call.
No other skill invocation may come between the grant and the call.
Right before every merge call, in the same turn, invoke `hivemind:merge-write` (Skill tool), with no other skill call between; a refused Skill call does not skip the merge call.

A refused merge call (a permission or auto-mode denial, not a script exit) is `MERGE=skipped:permission-denied`, routed the same with no retry; its `Next action` also names the rule `Bash(bash "<the script's full path>" *)` for `permissions.allow` in `.claude/settings.local.json`.
